main_text.p: Compositum augetur in simplici: ut compositum cum ἀν & δυς: sic ἀναγγέλλω ἀνήγγελμον, læta nuncio, bam. ἀνεργετέω ἀνηργέτεον, beneficio afficio, bam.
ἀνορχέω ἀνώρχεον, sanctè juro, bam: sic δυσαρεστέω δυσηρέστεον, morosus sum, e-ram.
δυσαπιστέω δυσηπίστεον, difficulter addu-cor ut non credam. Attamen

Derivata a nominibus sive simplicibus sive compositis, augentur in principio. A simplicibus, ut πλέω ἐπλεον, a πλος finis. A compositis, ut λυσιπλέω ἐλυσιπλέον, a λυσιπλὴς utilis. sic ἡκρολόγι σαχυας in Epigramm. ab ἀκρολογία: hoc autem ab ἀκρολόγος summa legens seu carpens. sic κατ' ἐμοῦ ψαλμο 68, ab ἀδολεσχέω: hoc autem ab ἀδόλεσχες garrulus, loquax. Idem fit in iis quæ deriuata sunt a nominibus compositis cum α, ut λωόμυσ, ἀδίκως, ab ἀνομία & ἀδικία: hæc autem ab ἄνομος leges transgrediens,

page.notes: Greek text is partly blurred and some accents are uncertain; the line "sic κατ' ἐμοῦ ψαλμο 68" and several Greek words in the last paragraph are doubtful and transcribed from the scan as best as legible. The Greek in the first lines (ἀν/δυς forms) is printed with worn letters.
